chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave-man may marry two free women, and he does not exceed (that number).
ai.seo_question: How many wives can a male slave marry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith specifies that a male slave (abd) is permitted to marry up to two free women (hurra'ayn), with the phrase 'la yazid' (he does not add) establishing a strict upper limit. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence, differentiating their marital capacity from the four wives allowed to free men, while emphasizing the requirement of the wives being free-born. The narration underscores the practical implications of social hierarchy within Islamic family law, ensuring clarity in the number of permissible spouses for those in servitude.
